title: Fixed Rear Pivot And Four Claw Staple Remover
description: One newly authored complete fixed open four-claw staple-remover exterior. Two short broad continuous fork-jaw bodies share a single rear transverse pin. Each jaw includes its own complete rear bridge, broad sloping body and two forward tapering finite blunt claws; the two pairs have different lateral spans and remain visibly separated in the fixed open pose. Two full broad finger-pressure covers root directly over the opposing short jaw backs, while independent side retaining caps finish the common pivot. Unlike the complete desktop stapler, there is no long magazine, staple channel, clincher anvil, ground sole or rear cradle on a base. Unlike the old combination pliers, there are no long crossed handle tangs, central crossover joint or serrated gripping faces. All geometric coordinates newly authored as one complete compact office hand tool; no old meshes extracted. One prop, zero scenes, four opaque untextured PBR roles. No staple, paper, cutting edge or demonstrated removal process. Fixed geometry only: no spring return, closing travel, staple engagement, force, pin bearing fit, finger fit, manufacture or safety claim. No rigging, animation or interaction made; outside static scope.
